incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2: tokenizer-preflight pods in cluster us-west-2 are OOM'ing and causing node flaps. Multiple pod restarts observed across nodepool-inference-1. Paging @alex (oncall). Impact: increased 5xx for text-generation routes and elevated tail latency.

alex (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking pod events. Any customer pages?

maria (support): Customer 'lexaai' reported ~30% error rate on batch inference since ~09:12 UTC; raised a support ticket referencing request IDs.

josh (runtime-eng): seeing repeated "killed by signal 9 (OOM)" in tokenizer container logs, but also interleaved CUDA errors in some pods: ``[E CudaDriver] CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`` followed by container restart. suspect large prompt preflight causing high CPU and occasionally triggering GPU faults due to memory pressure.

alex (oncall): kubectl top shows CPU spikes on tokenizer-preproc containers up to 95% then OOM. Here's partial output: ```kubectl top pods -n inference | grep tokenizer-preproc\ntokenizer-preproc-7f6c8    1100m   512Mi\ntokenizer-preproc-8g2k1    1200m   480Mi\n```

anika (sre): Node metrics show kernel OOM events at the same timestamps as the pod kills. Nodes A and C cycled. Likely CPU hotloop in parsing layer exhausting host memory (we run shared hostcache). We should cordon affected nodes and drain gracefully to stop further flaps.

kevin (infra): I'm cordoning node nodepool-inference-1-az1-0 now: ``kubectl cordon nodepool-inference-1-az1-0``. Will start rebalancing.

alex (oncall): Doing quick mitigations: 1) scale down tokenizer-preproc replica count to 2 to reduce pressure (will temporarily throttle throughput). 2) apply a short-term ingress token rate-limit to 5 r/s for text-gen route for customers on this cluster. 3) bounce a primed GPU pool to clear driver state.

josh (runtime-eng): For quick fix, push runtime change to disable aggressive token preflight (the new pre-scan that expands complex regexes) — setting ENV TOKEN_PRESCAN=false. Pushing a hotfix to deployment config now.

maria (support): Communicated to lexai about degraded performance and told them mitigation is in progress. They asked if long-running jobs will be killed — replied only new requests might be rate-limited, existing in-flight should finish if they land on stable nodes.

alex (oncall): Applied HPA override and scaled replicas: ``kubectl scale deploy tokenizer-preproc --replicas=2 -n inference``. Also set temporary ingress limiter: ``kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: ingress-rate-limit
  namespace: inference
spec: {}
EOF``
(placeholder for managed limiter — infra handled traffic shaping).

josh (runtime-eng): Confirmed environment toggle rolled to pods. New pods show lower CPU in the last 3 minutes. No new CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION in latest logs.

anika (sre): Node cordon + drain completed for nodepool-inference-1-az1-0. Drains moved other pods and we reduced eviction churn. Monitoring for 10m to ensure no more OOM.

kevin (infra): Restarted GPU daemonset on the affected hosts to clear lingering driver faults: ``kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-drivers -n infra``. We'll continue to monitor driver crash reports.

alex (oncall): Quick customer impact summary: lexai saw 30% error spike, other customers saw transient latency increases and small error rates. No data exfiltration or failed inference completions reported beyond retries. Marking impact as partial degradation, not outage.

luis (customer-success): Notifying key customers of mitigation steps and ETA for next update (~30m).

josh (runtime-eng): Root cause hypothesis: a recent tokenizer pre-scan optimization had a worst-case path for large prompts that causes exponential work (regex backtracking) at scale, driving CPU to host OOM, which then causes kernel/GPU driver instability and CUDA errors. Next steps: revert the optimization, add input-size safety checks, and add per-request CPU-bound watchdog.

anika (sre): Action items for post-incident: 1) revert prescan change in canary and run stress tests with large prompts. 2) Add CPU cgroup limit at pod-level to avoid host OOM. 3) Add alerting for preflight CPU hotloops (detect >80% CPU on tokenizer for >30s). 4) Create runbook update for tokenizer OOM.

alex (oncall): Handoff to @anika for the next 8h window. Current status: mitigations applied, errors trending down. I'll remain reachable for questions. Please keep this thread updated with any regression.

anika (sre): Acknowledged handoff. I'll coordinate the rollbacks and the postmortem. Leaving the temporary rate-limiter and replica cap active until prescan is reverted.

maria (support): I'll follow up with lexai and update the ticket once prescan is reverted.

josh (runtime-eng): Patch created: ``git rev 7fa3c1b`` — revert prescan and add input-length guard. Will open PR and request expedited review.

anika (sre): Noted. Creating incident timeline and will tag owners for each action. Next status update in 30 minutes or sooner if regressions. :white_check_mark:

luis (customer-success): Thanks team — customers appreciate the quick mitigation.

incident-bot: Incident marked as "stabilized" by alex (oncall). Open actions remain: prescan revert, stress test, runbook updates, and add cgroup limits.

alex (oncall): Closing active paging. Handoff complete. Good job team. :thumbsup:
